## Feature Request

**For English only**, other languages will not be accepted.

Please pay attention on issues you submitted, because we maybe need more details. 
If no response anymore and we cannot make decision by current information, we will **close it**.

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Currently, ShardingSphere-Proxy supports the basic packets required to perform transactions with Firebird. However, for full compatibility with the Firebird drivers, ShardingSphere-Proxy must support all Wire Protocol packets.

### Describe the feature you would like.

Add support for the Firebird Wire protocol packages listed below.

- [x] [Identification (connect)](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-op-connect) 
Pull request: #35937

- [x] [Simple accept](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-op-accept) 
Pull request: #35937

- [x] [Accept with data](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-op-accept-data) 
Pull request: #35937

- [ ] [Conditional accept](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-op-accept-data) 

- [ ] [Continue authentication](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-op-cont-auth) 

- [ ] [Trusted authentication](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-op-trusted-auth) 

- [ ] [Database encryption key callback](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-op-crypt-key-callback) 

- [ ] [Enable wire encryption](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-op-crypt) 

- [ ] [Connection rejection](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-op-reject) 

- [ ] [Disconnect](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-connect-disconnect) 

### Steps to implement Wire Protocol packet

1. Add packet to org.apache.shardingsphere.database.protocol.firebird module
2. Add executor for created packet to org.apache.shardingsphere.proxy.frontend.firebird module
3. Add exceptions to org.apache.shardingsphere.database.exception.firebird module if needed
4. Add unit tests for created classes.

## Feature Request

**For English only**, other languages will not be accepted.

Please pay attention on issues you submitted, because we maybe need more details. 
If no response anymore and we cannot make decision by current information, we will **close it**.

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Currently, ShardingSphere-Proxy supports the basic packets required to perform transactions with Firebird. However, for full compatibility with the Firebird drivers, ShardingSphere-Proxy must support all Wire Protocol packets.

### Describe the feature you would like.

Add support for the Firebird Wire protocol packages listed below.

- [x] [Attach database](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-databases-attach) 
Pull request: #35937

- [ ] [Create database](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-databases-create)

- [ ] [Drop](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-databases-drop) 

- [ ] [Detach](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-connect-detach) 

- [ ] [Database information request](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-databases-information) 
Partially resolved in: #35937. Support for all requested items must be added.

- [ ] [Cancellation](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-databases-cancel) 

### Steps to implement Wire Protocol packet

1. Add packet to org.apache.shardingsphere.database.protocol.firebird module
2. Add executor for created packet to org.apache.shardingsphere.proxy.frontend.firebird module
3. Add exceptions to org.apache.shardingsphere.database.exception.firebird module if needed
4. Add unit tests for created classes.

## Feature Request

**For English only**, other languages will not be accepted.

Please pay attention on issues you submitted, because we maybe need more details. 
If no response anymore and we cannot make decision by current information, we will **close it**.

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Currently, ShardingSphere-Proxy supports the basic packets required to perform transactions with Firebird. However, for full compatibility with the Firebird drivers, ShardingSphere-Proxy must support all Wire Protocol packets.

### Describe the feature you would like.

Add support for the Firebird Wire protocol packages listed below.

- [ ] [Connection request](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-events-connect-request) 

- [ ] [Queue events](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-events-que-events) 

- [ ] [Cancel events](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-events-cancel-events) 

- [ ] [Event notification](https://firebirdsql.org/file/documentation/html/en/firebirddocs/wireprotocol/firebird-wire-protocol.html#wireprotocol-events-notification) 

### Steps to implement Wire Protocol packet

1. Add packet to org.apache.shardingsphere.database.protocol.firebird module
2. Add executor for created packet to org.apache.shardingsphere.proxy.frontend.firebird module
3. Add exceptions to org.apache.shardingsphere.database.exception.firebird module if needed
4. Add unit tests for created classes.

body_text:
## Bug Report

### Which version of ShardingSphere did you use?

5.5.3 (binary distribution), Java 17.

### Which project did you use? ShardingSphere-JDBC or ShardingSphere-Proxy?

ShardingSphere-Proxy, PostgreSQL frontend protocol.

### Expected behavior

A join between non-binding sharded tables whose matching rows are on **different** data sources, with SQL federation disabled (the default), is either executed correctly or rejected with an error. The same applies to an `IN (subquery)` whose rows are on other data sources. The documentation says cross-instance joins need SQL federation.

### Actual behavior

Both statements run on each data source against only that data source's rows, and the partial results are merged. The client gets a wrong answer and no error or warning:

```
=> SELECT count(*) FROM t_other o JOIN t_sharded a ON a.id = o.ref_id;
 count
-------
   104          -- correct answer: 400 (every ref_id exists in t_sharded); the 4 data sources return 26 each

=> SELECT count(*) FROM t_sharded WHERE id IN (SELECT ref_id FROM t_other WHERE okey <= 10);
 count
-------
     2          -- correct answer: 10; the subquery is routed to ds_0, which holds only 2 of the 10 referenced ids
```

### Reason analyze (If you can)

Without federation, non-binding tables go through the standard/Cartesian route per data source, which can only see co-located rows. Nothing detects that the join condition spans data sources, so a partial result is returned. Possibly related: #38456 (routing of subqueries with non-binding tables).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior, such as: SQL to execute, sharding rule configuration, when exception occur etc.

```yaml
rules:
- !SHARDING
  tables:
    t_sharded:
      actualDataNodes: ds_${0..3}.t_sharded
      databaseStrategy:
        standard:
          shardingColumn: id
          shardingAlgorithmName: by_id
    t_other:
      actualDataNodes: ds_${0..3}.t_other
      databaseStrategy:
        standard:
          shardingColumn: okey
          shardingAlgorithmName: by_okey
  shardingAlgorithms:
    by_id:
      type: INLINE
      props:
        algorithm-expression: ds_${(id - 1).intdiv(100)}
    by_okey:
      type: INLINE
      props:
        algorithm-expression: ds_${(okey - 1).intdiv(100)}
```
4 PostgreSQL 18.6 data sources (`ds_0`..`ds_3`), rows id 1-100 / 101-200 / 201-300 / 301-400. `global.yaml`: Standalone mode, `proxy-frontend-database-protocol-type: PostgreSQL`, XA (Atomikos), SQL federation not enabled (default).

```sql
CREATE TABLE t_sharded (id int PRIMARY KEY, v int NOT NULL, s text);
CREATE TABLE t_other (okey int PRIMARY KEY, ref_id int NOT NULL);
-- t_sharded: id 1..400, v = id % 7, s = 'x' || id
-- t_other:   okey 1..400, ref_id = (okey * 37) % 400 + 1   (points to rows on other data sources)
```

Run the two statements above through the proxy.

### Suggestion

When SQL federation is disabled, raise an error (e.g. "cross-data-source join requires SQL federation") instead of returning per-data-source partial results.

{"repository": "apache/shardingsphere", "task_candidate_id": 1242, "repository_id": 31, "issue_number": 40196, "github_issue_id": 5856765445, "html_url": "https://github.com/apache/shardingsphere/issues/40196", "created_at": "2026-10-14T22:30:33+00:00", "author_association": "NONE", "title": "Proxy: join / IN subquery across data sources silently returns partial results when SQL federation is disabled", "body_text": "## Bug Report

### Which version of ShardingSphere did you use?

5.5.3 (binary distribution), Java 17.

### Which project did you use? ShardingSphere-JDBC or ShardingSphere-Proxy?

ShardingSphere-Proxy, PostgreSQL frontend protocol.

### Expected behavior

A join between non-binding sharded tables whose matching rows are on **different** data sources, with SQL federation disabled (the default), is either executed correctly or rejected with an error. The same applies to an `IN (subquery)` whose rows are on other data sources. The documentation says cross-instance joins need SQL federation.

### Actual behavior

Both statements run on each data source against only that data source's rows, and the partial results are merged. The client gets a wrong answer and no error or warning:

```
=> SELECT count(*) FROM t_other o JOIN t_sharded a ON a.id = o.ref_id;
 count
-------
   104          -- correct answer: 400 (every ref_id exists in t_sharded); the 4 data sources return 26 each

=> SELECT count(*) FROM t_sharded WHERE id IN (SELECT ref_id FROM t_other WHERE okey <= 10);
 count
-------
     2          -- correct answer: 10; the subquery is routed to ds_0, which holds only 2 of the 10 referenced ids
```

### Reason analyze (If you can)

Without federation, non-binding tables go through the standard/Cartesian route per data source, which can only see co-located rows. Nothing detects that the join condition spans data sources, so a partial result is returned. Possibly related: #38456 (routing of subqueries with non-binding tables).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior, such as: SQL to execute, sharding rule configuration, when exception occur etc.

```yaml
rules:
- !SHARDING
  tables:
    t_sharded:
      actualDataNodes: ds_${0..3}.t_sharded
      databaseStrategy:
        standard:
          shardingColumn: id
          shardingAlgorithmName: by_id
    t_other:
      actualDataNodes: ds_${0..3}.t_other
      databaseStrategy:
        standard:
          shardingColumn: okey
          shardingAlgorithmName: by_okey
  shardingAlgorithms:
    by_id:
      type: INLINE
      props:
        algorithm-expression: ds_${(id - 1).intdiv(100)}
    by_okey:
      type: INLINE
      props:
        algorithm-expression: ds_${(okey - 1).intdiv(100)}
```
4 PostgreSQL 18.6 data sources (`ds_0`..`ds_3`), rows id 1-100 / 101-200 / 201-300 / 301-400. `global.yaml`: Standalone mode, `proxy-frontend-database-protocol-type: PostgreSQL`, XA (Atomikos), SQL federation not enabled (default).

```sql
CREATE TABLE t_sharded (id int PRIMARY KEY, v int NOT NULL, s text);
CREATE TABLE t_other (okey int PRIMARY KEY, ref_id int NOT NULL);
-- t_sharded: id 1..400, v = id % 7, s = 'x' || id
-- t_other:   okey 1..400, ref_id = (okey * 37) % 400 + 1   (points to rows on other data sources)
```

Run the two statements above through the proxy.

### Suggestion

When SQL federation is disabled, raise an error (e.g. "cross-data-source join requires SQL federation") instead of returning per-data-source partial results.

## Background

Motan runtime code and its Spring Boot starter were copied to `apache/shenyu-plugin-store` in PRs [#1](https://github.com/apache/shenyu-plugin-store/pull/1) and [#3](https://github.com/apache/shenyu-plugin-store/pull/3). The main repository later removed Motan support in commit [338ea9adaf](https://github.com/apache/shenyu/commit/338ea9adaf), but the store copy still depends on Motan-specific classes removed from ShenYu core, including `PluginEnum.MOTAN`, `RpcTypeEnum.MOTAN`, Motan DTOs/constants, and result codes.

The migration is therefore present as source code but is not yet a buildable, releasable, or E2E-verified external plugin.

Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Rebase the Motan plugin and starter onto the supported ShenYu external-plugin API.
- Move Motan-owned identifiers, configuration DTOs, result mapping, and protocol constants out of ShenYu core dependencies or replace them with the agreed generic extension contract.
- Retain Spring Boot 2/3 auto-configuration metadata only where it matches the supported compatibility matrix.
- Restore and expand unit tests for plugin execution, metadata/config refresh, proxy/cache lifecycle, and starter loading.
- Add a real E2E scenario with a Motan provider, gateway, admin/config setup, successful invocation, invalid metadata/body handling, and config refresh.
- Document Motan and JDK/framework compatibility and mark the plugin maintenance status clearly.

### apache/shenyu and companion repositories

- Remove stale Motan dependency-governance and distribution LICENSE entries that were reintroduced after the source removal; retain historical release notes and upgrade SQL.
- Decide whether client registration remains supported. If yes, maintain it in the authoritative client repository and cover registration-to-invocation E2E; if no, document manual metadata registration.
- Ensure no current distribution or default bootstrap contains Motan artifacts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Motan plugin and starter build against the declared ShenYu release without restored Motan-specific core enums/DTOs.
- [ ] Unit tests run in CI and cover success, failure, metadata refresh, and resource cleanup.
- [ ] E2E starts a real Motan provider and proves gateway invocation and dynamic config update.
- [ ] The produced artifacts can be consumed by a minimal ShenYu bootstrap.
- [ ] Main-repository stale docs/licenses are cleaned without rewriting historical migrations.
- [ ] Support/deprecation status and rollback instructions are documented.

## Background

TARS plugin and starter snapshots already exist in `apache/shenyu-plugin-store` through PRs [#2](https://github.com/apache/shenyu-plugin-store/pull/2) and [#3](https://github.com/apache/shenyu-plugin-store/pull/3). They are not yet the authoritative implementation:

- the store copy predates recent fixes in `apache/shenyu`;
- the store TARS POM explicitly skips Surefire tests;
- there is no TARS E2E workflow in the store;
- the implementation still depends on TARS-specific core enums, DTOs, constants, response handling, admin registration, and client modules;
- open bug #6738 must not be lost during the move.

Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Port all TARS changes made in `apache/shenyu` after plugin-store PR #2, including proxy initialization, empty proxy-list handling, selector/upstream updates, null handling, and resource cleanup fixes.
- Remove the Surefire skip and make the existing plugin/starter tests pass in CI.
- Add regression coverage for #6738 and every post-copy TARS fix.
- Add a TARS E2E environment covering provider startup, client/API registration or explicit metadata registration, selector/rule creation, successful invocation, no-result handling, failure handling, and dynamic metadata/config refresh.
- Add documentation and an example bootstrap that consumes the external starter.

### apache/shenyu and client/admin boundaries

- Replace hard-coded `PluginEnum.TARS`, `RpcTypeEnum.TARS`, RPC response-writer entries, TARS DTOs/converters, and admin registration dependencies with the external-plugin contract.
- Move or preserve TARS client registration in the authoritative client repository; do not leave duplicate published artifacts.
- Remove TARS plugin/starter/default-bootstrap dependencies, examples, and duplicated integration tests from the main repository only after store parity passes.
- Keep historical upgrade SQL; add a migration/compatibility note for existing TARS plugin data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Store TARS source contains all fixes present on main at cutover time.
- [ ] Unit and starter tests run rather than being skipped.
- [ ] #6738 has a regression test and is resolved or explicitly carried as a blocker.
- [ ] E2E proves registration/metadata, invocation, failure behavior, and hot config refresh.
- [ ] A minimal ShenYu bootstrap works with the plugin-store TARS starter.
- [ ] Maven publication ownership is switched atomically with no duplicate coordinates.
- [ ] Main-repository removal occurs only after the external artifact and E2E are green.

body_text:
## Background

ShenYu still ships `shenyu-plugin-hystrix` and its starter in the default bootstrap. The module uses Hystrix `1.5.18`, whose upstream project is in maintenance mode and states that no new releases, issue reviews, or PR merges are planned. Upstream recommends Resilience4j for new applications.

This migration should preserve a compatibility path for existing users while removing an end-of-life implementation from the main repository. It must be presented as a deprecated legacy plugin, not as a recommended fault-tolerance option.

Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add the Hystrix runtime plugin and Spring Boot starter under a clearly documented legacy/deprecated section.
- Port all existing unit tests and the latest shared NPE/config-handling fixes.
- Add tests for thread and semaphore isolation, timeout, fallback, circuit opening, rule updates, metrics cleanup, and executor/thread-pool shutdown.
- Add an E2E case that proves success, timeout/fallback, circuit-breaker behavior, and dynamic rule refresh against a deliberately slow/failing upstream.
- Document the final upstream version, known limitations, supported ShenYu versions, and migration guidance to Resilience4j.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove Hystrix plugin/starter/default-bootstrap dependencies only after the external artifact is released and verified.
- Move Hystrix-specific active configuration/DTO ownership out of core where required by the external-plugin contract.
- Keep historical database upgrade SQL; update current seed data, menus, docs, examples, metrics references, LICENSE/NOTICE, and distribution packaging.
- Add release notes and a configuration mapping guide from Hystrix to Resilience4j.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The plugin-store artifact preserves existing Hystrix configuration semantics for the supported compatibility line.
- [ ] Unit tests cover isolation, timeout, fallback, circuit state, config refresh, and cleanup.
- [ ] E2E verifies timeout/fallback and circuit behavior with a real gateway.
- [ ] Documentation prominently marks the plugin deprecated and recommends Resilience4j.
- [ ] Existing users have a tested migration guide.
- [ ] Main-repository removal happens only after the external artifact is available.
- [ ] No Hystrix dependency remains in the default ShenYu distribution.

## Background

Casdoor is a vendor-specific IAM integration that is not required by the ShenYu request-processing core. Its implementation and starter are small and independently loadable, but current packaging includes them in the main build and default bootstrap.

Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add the Casdoor runtime plugin and Spring Boot starter.
- Move Casdoor-owned configuration and handler logic while depending only on the supported ShenYu plugin API.
- Port existing unit tests and add coverage for plugin-data refresh, missing/invalid token, callback parameters, downstream identity headers, authentication failure, and client/resource cleanup.
- Add an E2E environment using a reproducible local Casdoor service or container. Cover login/token validation, unauthorized access, identity propagation, selector/rule matching, and runtime configuration refresh.
- Document required Casdoor configuration, certificates/secrets, supported versions, and secure production defaults.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove the Casdoor plugin/starter and default-bootstrap dependency after store parity.
- Update current admin seed data, plugin menu/permissions, dependency management, docs, LICENSE/NOTICE, and distribution packaging.
- Preserve historical upgrade SQL; provide a current-version migration path for existing plugin configuration.
- Ensure no Casdoor SDK is pulled into the default bootstrap after cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Plugin and starter compile against the declared ShenYu plugin API.
- [ ] Unit tests cover authentication success/failure, config refresh, and trusted identity propagation.
- [ ] E2E runs without external shared credentials and validates a real authentication flow.
- [ ] Secrets/certificates are never committed or logged.
- [ ] Existing admin configuration can be migrated or reused with documented steps.
- [ ] The default ShenYu distribution no longer includes the Casdoor SDK.
- [ ] Store publication and main-repository removal are coordinated and rollback-safe.

## Background

`shenyu-plugin-logging-aliyun-sls` is a vendor-specific logging sink built on the shared ShenYu logging abstraction. It is not required by gateway core and should be released from the extension repository with its own dependency and compatibility lifecycle.

Related lifecycle issue: #6655. Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add the Aliyun SLS logging plugin and Spring Boot starter while consuming the supported `shenyu-plugin-logging-common` artifact.
- Port current main-branch fixes, including configuration-refresh behavior, client-init failure handling, time-unit correctness, and shutdown behavior.
- Port and expand unit tests for configuration parsing, payload mapping, batching, retry/failure behavior, config refresh, start/stop idempotency, and resource cleanup.
- Add a credential-free PR E2E/contract test using a local controllable endpoint or SDK test double that verifies a gateway access log reaches the sink boundary.
- Optionally add a secret-gated scheduled smoke test against a real SLS project; it must not be required for contributor PRs.
- Document endpoint, project/logstore, credential injection, payload schema, retry behavior, and supported versions.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove the plugin/starter/default-bootstrap dependency after store parity.
- Update PluginEnum/current admin seed data, menus, docs, dependency management, LICENSE/NOTICE, and distribution packaging.
- Preserve historical upgrade SQL and document how existing selector/plugin configuration continues to work.
- Ensure the default distribution no longer pulls the Aliyun SLS SDK.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests cover config refresh, batching/error paths, and client lifecycle.
- [ ] PR E2E is deterministic and needs no cloud credentials.
- [ ] Optional real-cloud smoke tests keep secrets in GitHub environments only.
- [ ] A minimal gateway can emit an access log through the external starter.
- [ ] #6655 is fixed or guarded by a regression test before cutover.
- [ ] Artifact publication and main-repository removal do not overlap.

## Background

`shenyu-plugin-logging-tencent-cls` is a Tencent Cloud-specific access-log sink. Its runtime is isolated behind `logging-common`, so ownership belongs in the plugin store rather than the gateway core repository.

Related lifecycle issue: #6655. Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add the Tencent CLS logging plugin and Spring Boot starter.
- Port all current fixes for configuration refresh, client initialization failures, time-unit conversion, asynchronous delivery, and shutdown.
- Add unit tests for configuration validation, log-event mapping, topic/logset selection, batching, retry/error handling, dynamic config refresh, repeated start, and client cleanup.
- Add a credential-free E2E/contract test with a local endpoint or SDK test double that proves gateway access logs reach the CLS client boundary.
- Optionally add a secret-gated scheduled real-CLS smoke test.
- Document credentials, region/endpoint, logset/topic configuration, payload fields, retry semantics, and supported versions.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove plugin/starter/default-bootstrap dependencies after parity.
- Update current enum/admin seed/menu/docs/dependency/license/distribution entries while retaining historical upgrade scripts.
- Ensure the default bootstrap no longer contains the Tencent CLS SDK.
- Add migration notes for existing selector and plugin configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests cover mapping, refresh, retry/failure, repeated start, and shutdown.
- [ ] PR E2E requires no external account or long-lived secret.
- [ ] Optional cloud smoke credentials are isolated and masked.
- [ ] The external starter works with a minimal ShenYu bootstrap.
- [ ] #6655 has regression coverage before cutover.
- [ ] Publication ownership is switched without duplicate artifacts.

## Background

`shenyu-plugin-logging-huawei-lts` is a Huawei Cloud-specific logging sink and is not part of the ShenYu core request path. It has recent configuration and long-log handling fixes that must be preserved during migration.

Related lifecycle issue: #6655. Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add the Huawei LTS logging plugin and Spring Boot starter.
- Port all current main-branch behavior, including generic Huawei configuration fields, extra-long-log handling, client-init failure handling, time-unit correctness, and shutdown.
- Add unit tests for configuration validation, log-group/stream mapping, long-log policy, batching, retry/failure, dynamic refresh, repeated start, and cleanup.
- Add a credential-free PR E2E/contract test using a local controllable endpoint or SDK abstraction.
- Optionally add a secret-gated scheduled LTS smoke test.
- Document authentication, region/endpoint, log group/stream, long-log behavior, payload schema, and supported SDK/ShenYu versions.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove plugin/starter/default-bootstrap dependencies after store parity.
- Update current enum/admin seed/menu/docs/dependency/license/distribution entries, retaining historical upgrade SQL.
- Ensure the default distribution no longer contains Huawei LTS SDK artifacts.
- Document migration of existing plugin configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Recent Huawei-specific fixes are present and regression-tested in the store.
- [ ] Unit tests cover long logs, refresh, failure, repeated start, and shutdown.
- [ ] PR E2E uses no real cloud credentials.
- [ ] Optional real-cloud checks keep credentials in protected GitHub environments.
- [ ] A minimal gateway emits logs through the external starter.
- [ ] #6655 has lifecycle regression coverage before cutover.
- [ ] Artifact publication and main removal are coordinated.

## Background

Apache Pulsar is active infrastructure, but `shenyu-plugin-logging-pulsar` is an optional sink adapter rather than gateway-core behavior. The migration is about repository ownership and dependency isolation, not ecosystem deprecation.

Related lifecycle issue: #6655. Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add the Pulsar logging plugin and Spring Boot starter while consuming the supported `logging-common` API.
- Port current fixes, including duplicate shutdown-hook removal and client-init failure handling.
- Port and expand unit tests for producer configuration, topic selection, event serialization, batching, send failure, broker unavailability/recovery, dynamic config refresh, repeated start, and shutdown.
- Add Testcontainers-based E2E with a real Pulsar broker. Start a gateway with the external starter, generate traffic, consume and assert the access-log event, update plugin configuration, and verify clean shutdown.
- Document broker/auth/TLS configuration, payload schema, delivery guarantees, backpressure/retry behavior, and version compatibility.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove the Pulsar logging plugin/starter/default-bootstrap dependency after parity.
- Update current enum/admin seed/menu/docs/dependency/license/distribution entries while keeping historical SQL.
- Ensure the default distribution no longer pulls Pulsar client artifacts.
- Document existing selector/config migration and artifact coordinates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests cover serialization, refresh, broker failure/recovery, repeated start, and cleanup.
- [ ] E2E uses a real disposable Pulsar broker and verifies the emitted record.
- [ ] Shutdown leaves no duplicate hook, producer, or executor.
- [ ] #6655 is fixed or protected by regression coverage.
- [ ] The external starter works with a minimal bootstrap.
- [ ] Store publication precedes coordinated main-repository removal.

## Background

ClickHouse is actively maintained, but `shenyu-plugin-logging-clickhouse` is an optional persistence sink. Moving it isolates its client dependency and release cadence from ShenYu core while preserving official support.

Related lifecycle issue: #6655. Historical data-mapping issue: #5229. Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add the ClickHouse logging plugin and Spring Boot starter using the supported `logging-common` API.
- Port current fixes for null/blank TTL configuration, config refresh, client-init failure handling, and shutdown.
- Port and expand unit tests for DDL/config generation, schema and status mapping, TTL handling, event serialization, batching, write failure, config refresh, repeated start, and cleanup.
- Add Testcontainers-based E2E with a real ClickHouse server. Generate gateway traffic, query the stored record, verify status/header/body fields, update configuration, and verify shutdown.
- Document schema ownership/migration, table and TTL settings, credentials/TLS, retention, supported versions, and upgrade compatibility.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove plugin/starter/default-bootstrap dependencies after store parity.
- Update current enum/admin seed/menu/docs/dependency/license/distribution entries while preserving historical upgrade SQL.
- Ensure the default distribution no longer contains the ClickHouse client.
- Publish migration notes for existing tables and plugin configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests cover TTL edge cases, mapping, refresh, failures, repeated start, and cleanup.
- [ ] E2E persists and queries a real access-log row in disposable ClickHouse.
- [ ] Regression coverage preserves the corrected status-field behavior from #5229.
- [ ] #6655 is fixed or guarded by lifecycle tests.
- [ ] Existing schemas/configurations have documented upgrade steps.
- [ ] Publication ownership and main-repository removal are coordinated.

body_text:
## Background

Polaris is not a single runtime plugin. ShenYu support spans admin listener, data-sync client, registry integration, Spring Boot starter, configuration, tests, and default-bootstrap dependencies. Its ecosystem is narrower than the default HTTP/WebSocket/ZooKeeper/Nacos paths, so it should be maintained as an optional extension stack.

This task intentionally treats Polaris as one vertical integration and must not move only one Maven module.

Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add an agreed top-level layout for non-request plugins/extensions.
- Migrate the Polaris admin listener, gateway data-sync module, registry/instance integration, Spring Boot starter, configuration objects, and all owned tests.
- Preserve current namespace, cache-removal, reconnect, watcher, and delete-event behavior.
- Add unit tests for serialization/path handling, listener updates/deletes, namespace isolation, reconnect, watcher cleanup, and close/shutdown.
- Add an integration/E2E environment with a disposable Polaris server, ShenYu admin, and gateway. Verify initial sync, plugin/selector/rule create-update-delete, namespace isolation, reconnect/recovery, and clean shutdown.
- Document Polaris server/client versions, authentication, namespace mapping, deployment, and ShenYu compatibility.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove all four Polaris integration surfaces and the default-bootstrap starter only after external parity: admin listener, sync-data-center, registry/instance support, and starter.
- Update dependency management, configuration docs, examples, CI matrices, LICENSE/NOTICE, and distribution packaging.
- Preserve historical upgrade/configuration documentation and add a cutover guide.
- Confirm that removing Polaris does not affect default HTTP/WebSocket or other sync channels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The complete Polaris vertical stack is owned and built in one repository.
- [ ] Unit tests cover create/update/delete, namespace isolation, reconnect, and cleanup.
- [ ] E2E proves admin-to-gateway synchronization through a real disposable Polaris service.
- [ ] Default sync channels pass regression tests after main-repository removal.
- [ ] A minimal gateway can enable Polaris solely by adding the external starter.
- [ ] Artifact publication and removal are rollback-safe and do not duplicate coordinates.

## Goal

Move selected optional ShenYu integrations from the main repository to `apache/shenyu-plugin-store` without losing behavior, tests, release ownership, documentation, or upgrade compatibility. Each plugin/integration is handled by its own issue and two-repository cutover.

Target repository: https://github.com/apache/shenyu-plugin-store

## Decision Principles

A module is a migration candidate when most of the following hold:

- it is not required by the generic request-processing or default data-sync path;
- it is a vendor-, middleware-, or protocol-specific adapter;
- it can be loaded through a starter/external-plugin contract;
- its dependency and release lifecycle should not enlarge the default distribution;
- behavior can be preserved by unit and real E2E coverage in the owning repository.

Migration does **not** mean abandonment. TARS, SOFA, Pulsar, ClickHouse, RabbitMQ, cloud logging, Casdoor, Polaris, and Consul remain supported extensions. Hystrix is the exception: it is migrated only as a deprecated legacy compatibility plugin because upstream is in maintenance mode.

## Mandatory Cutover Contract

Every child issue must satisfy all gates before source removal from `apache/shenyu`:

1. **Foundation**: plugin-store builds from a clean checkout with wrapper, CI, Checkstyle, RAT, unit tests, packaging, and compatibility rules.
2. **Parity**: all main-branch fixes at the cutover commit are present in the store.
3. **Core decoupling**: optional plugin identifiers, DTOs, converters, response handlers, and admin metadata no longer require hard-coded core implementation dependencies, or a documented stable compatibility contract exists.
4. **Tests**: unit and starter auto-configuration tests run and are not skipped.
5. **E2E**: a real gateway plus disposable/mock external service proves success, failure, config refresh, and clean shutdown. Cloud-vendor PR tests must not require shared credentials.
6. **Release**: exactly one repository publishes each Maven coordinate; source/javadoc/signing/LICENSE/NOTICE requirements pass.
7. **Main cleanup**: remove active modules, aggregators, default-bootstrap dependencies, current seed/menu/config entries, examples, duplicate tests, and distribution dependencies. Keep historical release notes and upgrade SQL.
8. **Rollback**: document how to return to the previous artifact/configuration during one supported release window.

Use one plugin migration per PR. A child issue may use separate preparation, store-addition, and main-removal PRs, but the removal PR must remain blocked until store artifacts and E2E are green.

## Phase 0: Make the Store a Valid Build Target

- [ ] #7294

## Phase 1: Complete Existing Store Migrations and Legacy Isolation

- [ ] #7295
- [ ] #7296
- [ ] #7298

## Phase 2: Move Leaf Authentication and Logging Adapters

- [ ] #7299
- [ ] #7300
- [ ] #7301
- [ ] #7302
- [ ] #7303
- [ ] #7304
- [ ] #7307

## Phase 3: Move Vertically Coupled Integrations

- [ ] #7297
- [ ] #7305
- [ ] #7308

## Scope Kept in the Main Repository for This Plan

- Dubbo, gRPC, Divide/Spring Cloud, and WebSocket proxy paths.
- Core plugin API/base/http client and request/response/routing transformations.
- Rate limiter and Resilience4j.
- Logging common/console and, initially, Kafka/Elasticsearch reference sinks.
- HTTP/WebSocket/ZooKeeper/Nacos data-sync paths.
- MQTT, TCP, and RocketMQ logging remain pending real usage/maintainer data and are not part of this migration batch.

## Program Completion Criteria

- [ ] All selected integrations have a documented owner and compatibility range.
- [ ] Main ShenYu builds and all affected regression suites pass without their source modules.
- [ ] The default bootstrap no longer includes migrated third-party SDKs.
- [ ] Plugin-store CI and release validation pass for every migrated module.
- [ ] Website/user documentation points to external coordinates and configuration.
- [ ] No artifact is published by both repositories for the same version.

## Background

`shenyu-plugin-logging-rabbitmq` is an optional access-log sink built on the shared ShenYu logging abstraction. It is not required by gateway core and should have an independent dependency and release lifecycle in `apache/shenyu-plugin-store`.

The current implementation has recent lifecycle fixes, including closing the connection when channel shutdown fails. Those changes and the shared collector lifecycle issue must be preserved during migration.

Tracked by #7306. Depends on #7294. Related lifecycle issue: #6655.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add the RabbitMQ logging plugin and Spring Boot starter while consuming the supported `shenyu-plugin-logging-common` artifact.
- Port every main-branch RabbitMQ fix present at the cutover commit.
- Port and expand unit tests for connection/channel creation, exchange/queue/routing-key configuration, event serialization, batching, publish confirms/failures, dynamic config refresh, repeated start, reconnect, and shutdown.
- Add Testcontainers-based E2E with a real RabbitMQ broker:
  - start a gateway with the external starter;
  - generate gateway traffic;
  - consume and validate the emitted access-log message;
  - update plugin configuration and verify the new destination;
  - restart or interrupt the broker and verify recovery;
  - verify clean gateway shutdown without leaked channels, connections, executors, or consumer threads.
- Document broker/TLS/authentication settings, exchange/queue requirements, payload schema, delivery guarantees, retry/backpressure behavior, and ShenYu/RabbitMQ compatibility.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove the RabbitMQ plugin, starter, aggregator entries, and default-bootstrap dependency only after store parity and artifact publication.
- Update current plugin enum/admin seed/menu/configuration, documentation, dependency management, LICENSE/NOTICE, and distribution packaging.
- Preserve historical release notes and upgrade SQL.
- Ensure the default ShenYu distribution no longer pulls the RabbitMQ Java client.
- Document migration of existing plugin/selector configuration and Maven coordinates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Store source contains all RabbitMQ fixes from main at the cutover commit.
- [ ] Unit tests cover mapping, publish failure, config refresh, repeated start, reconnect, and cleanup.
- [ ] E2E uses a disposable real RabbitMQ broker and validates the emitted message.
- [ ] Broker restart/recovery and clean shutdown are covered.
- [ ] #6655 is fixed or protected by regression tests before cutover.
- [ ] A minimal gateway can emit logs by adding only the external starter and configuration.
- [ ] Exactly one repository publishes each RabbitMQ plugin artifact version.
- [ ] Main-repository removal occurs only after plugin-store CI and E2E are green.

body_text:
## Background

Consul support is an optional vertical integration rather than one request plugin. The current implementation spans:

- `shenyu-admin-listener-consul`;
- `shenyu-sync-data-consul`;
- `shenyu-registry-consul`;
- `shenyu-spring-boot-starter-sync-data-consul`;
- the admin and default-bootstrap dependency graphs.

Moving only one module would leave a split owner and an untestable configuration path. The entire Consul stack must move as one migration unit.

Tracked by #7306. Depends on #7294.

## Scope

### plugin-store

- Add a supported top-level layout for admin listeners, data-sync adapters, registry/instance adapters, and sync starters.
- Migrate all four Consul modules with their current unit tests.
- Preserve all fixes present at cutover, including concurrent watcher state, registry executor shutdown, instance watcher consistency, multi-selector/multi-registry behavior, update detection, and resource cleanup.
- Add missing starter auto-configuration tests.
- Add a Testcontainers-based integration/E2E environment using a real disposable Consul server, ShenYu admin, and ShenYu gateway.
- Cover:
  - initial plugin/selector/rule synchronization;
  - create, update, and delete propagation;
  - namespace/key-prefix isolation;
  - watch interruption and reconnect/recovery;
  - service instance register, update, deregister, and discovery;
  - multiple selectors or registry endpoints;
  - orderly shutdown without leaked watcher/executor threads.
- Document Consul ACL/TLS/datacenter configuration, key layout, supported Consul/client versions, licensing considerations for the test/runtime environment, and ShenYu compatibility.

### apache/shenyu

- Remove the Consul admin-listener dependency from admin, sync-data module, registry module, sync starter, aggregator entries, and default-bootstrap dependency only after external parity.
- Update dependency management, configuration metadata, examples, docs, CI matrices, LICENSE/NOTICE, and distribution packaging.
- Preserve historical release notes and upgrade/configuration documentation.
- Confirm HTTP, WebSocket, ZooKeeper, Nacos, and other sync/registry implementations pass regression tests after removal.
- Provide a migration and rollback guide for existing Consul keyspaces and gateway/admin configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Admin listener, data sync, registry/instance support, and starter are owned and built together in plugin-store.
- [ ] Unit tests cover create/update/delete, watcher concurrency, reconnect, instance updates, and shutdown.
- [ ] Starter auto-configuration has direct test coverage.
- [ ] E2E proves admin-to-gateway synchronization and instance registration through a real Consul server.
- [ ] Other sync and registry implementations remain green after main-repository removal.
- [ ] Existing Consul key layout/configuration has documented compatibility and rollback steps.
- [ ] A minimal admin/gateway deployment can enable Consul solely through external artifacts and configuration.
- [ ] Artifact publication and main-repository removal are coordinated without duplicate coordinates.
